title: How do you build a training matrix for an energy utility?
seoTitle: Training matrix for an energy utility
description: Build an energy utility training matrix: NERC CIP, SOCI, NIS2, pipeline, water and nuclear operator duties by role, with access gates, clocks and evidence.
shortAnswer: An energy utility training matrix lists control room, field, operational technology, security and governance roles against the duties of each regime the utility falls under, such as NERC CIP-004 for bulk electric system access, PHMSA operator qualification for pipelines, state water operator certification, the SOCI Act in Australia and NIS2 in the EU. Each cell records whether training gates access, the clock the rule sets, and the record the auditor will request.
keyTakeaways: Utility rules often make training a condition of access or of performing a task: NERC CIP-004-7 requires role based training before authorized access, and PHMSA requires covered task qualification before the work.

Utilities carry some of the most precise clocks in any matrix: quarterly security awareness and 15 calendar month training under CIP-004-7, a 24 month requalification cycle with an annual operating test for licensed reactor operators.
Other utility regimes set outcomes, not intervals. PHMSA leaves evaluation intervals to the operator, and the SOCI CIRMP Rules never use the word training.
Contractors and vendors with access to critical systems need their own rows, because CIP-004, PHMSA and the SOCI Rules all reach beyond employees.
CIP-004-8, the enhanced SOCI risk management rules and national NIS2 laws are all moving through implementation, so several cells need future dated versions.

sections.heading: What makes an energy utility training matrix different?

blocks.text: Many of its cells are gates rather than reminders: a person may not receive access to a cyber system, perform a pipeline task or run a treatment plant shift until the training or qualification is complete. A matrix that only tracks due dates misses the point, because the control is the access decision.

Utility duties also fall into three distinct kinds. Some are personal credentials held by the individual, such as a water operator certificate or a reactor operator license. Some are program duties on the utility, such as a pipeline operator qualification program. Some are governance duties on the board or management body, such as NIS2 Article 20. The general method in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) still applies, but each column should record which of the three kinds it is, because that decides who holds the evidence.

sections.heading: Which utility roles should become rows?

blocks.text: Build rows around access and task, because utility rules attach duties to who can reach a system or perform a defined task. Job titles vary between electricity, gas and water businesses, but the access patterns repeat.

sections.heading: Which training duties apply to utilities in each market?

blocks.text: The columns below come from the library's regulation pages, as at November 2026. Each link opens the full requirement.

items: **United States, electricity.** NERC Reliability Standard CIP-004-7, overseen by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), applies to balancing authorities, generator owners and operators, reliability coordinators, transmission owners and operators, and some distribution providers. Requirement R1 Part 1.1 requires security awareness at least once each calendar quarter for personnel with authorized electronic or unescorted physical access, and R2 requires role based training on nine topics before access and at least once every 15 calendar months ([NERC CIP-004](/regulations/nerc-cip-004-training-requirements)).

**United States, gas and liquids pipelines.** The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) requires a written operator qualification program. A qualified individual has been evaluated and can perform the covered task and recognize and react to abnormal operating conditions ([PHMSA operator qualification](/regulations/pipeline-operator-qualification-requirements)).

**United States, water.** Community and nontransient noncommunity water systems need certified operators under state programs that meet EPA's 1999 guidelines, including a designated certified operator available for each operating shift and renewal on a cycle of no more than three years with state approved training ([drinking water operator certification](/regulations/drinking-water-operator-certification-requirements)).

**United States, nuclear generation.** 10 CFR 50.120 requires a training program derived from a systems approach to training for nine categories of non-licensed and support personnel, and 10 CFR 55.59 sets requalification for licensed operators ([NRC plant personnel training](/regulations/nrc-nuclear-power-plant-personnel-training)).

**Australia.** The Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 requires responsible entities for critical electricity, gas, liquid fuel and energy market operator assets to keep a risk management program. Section 9 of the CIRMP Rules requires them to identify critical workers, permit access to critical components only after a suitability assessment, and minimize risks from malicious or negligent employees and contractors ([SOCI Act](/regulations/soci-act-critical-infrastructure-personnel-training)).

**European Union and Portugal.** Energy is a NIS2 sector. Article 20(2) requires management body members of essential and important entities to follow cybersecurity training, and Article 21(2)(g) lists basic cyber hygiene and cybersecurity training as a minimum risk management measure. Portugal transposed NIS2 through Decree-Law 125/2025, in force from April 3, 2026 ([NIS2](/regulations/nis2-management-body-training)).

blocks.title: Check before adding a lockout row
blocks.text: OSHA's general industry lockout/tagout standard, 29 CFR 1910.147, excludes electric utility generation, transmission and distribution installations in paragraph (a)(1)(ii). Do not map network field crews to it by default; see the [lockout/tagout page](/regulations/osha-lockout-tagout-training-requirements) for its scope.

sections.heading: What does a utility training matrix look like with real rows?

blocks.text: It looks like a register where each row states the gate, the clock and the record. The extract below is illustrative only, for a hypothetical multi-utility with a US transmission business, a gas distribution pipeline, a Texas water system, an Australian electricity asset and a Portuguese subsidiary. Frequencies labelled utility policy are choices the utility made and must justify; the rest are stated in the cited rule.

sections.heading: Which utility training intervals are fixed by rule?

blocks.text: Electricity cyber security and nuclear operator licensing fix their clocks precisely; pipeline qualification and critical infrastructure risk programs leave them to the utility. Write each fixed clock in the matrix exactly as the rule states it.

items: **Calendar quarter and 15 calendar months.** CIP-004-7 counts in calendar quarters and calendar months, not rolling years, so a 12 month default would be stricter than needed in one place and wrong in format everywhere.

**24 months and every year.** 10 CFR 55.59 runs requalification as a continuous cycle of no more than two years, with a comprehensive written examination and an annual operating test. Active status also requires seven 8 hour or five 12 hour shifts per calendar quarter under 55.53(e).
**Three years or less.** EPA's guidelines require water operator renewal on a fixed cycle not exceeding three years, and reexamination if a certificate has been expired for more than two years.

**Operator set.** PHMSA requires the operator to identify each covered task and the interval at which evaluation is needed, and its program must provide for evaluation after an incident. Record the reasoning for each interval. The guide on [setting mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) covers how.

sections.heading: What records will utility auditors and inspectors ask for?

blocks.text: They ask for records that prove the gate held: training completed before access, qualification current on the date of the task, and evaluation methods that meet the rule. Retention differs by regime, so store it per row.

What must be kept

blocks.text: Method matters as much as retention. Since December 16, 2004, PHMSA has not allowed observation of on the job performance as the sole evaluation method, and 10 CFR 55.4 defines a systems approach to training that includes evaluating trainee mastery. See [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency) for how practical assessment fits alongside written tests.

sections.heading: Which utility rules are changing in 2026 and beyond?

blocks.text: Three regimes in the matrix were mid transition as at November 2026, so give each affected row a dated successor.

items: **CIP-004-8, United States.** FERC Order No. 919 approved CIP-004-8, effective May 26, 2026. NERC's implementation plan makes it enforceable on the first day of the first calendar quarter 24 months after approval, so CIP-004-7 remains operative for now. CIP-004-8 adds Shared Cyber Infrastructure and medium impact systems with Interactive Remote Access to the training parts, keeping the quarterly and 15 calendar month intervals.

**Enhanced SOCI rules, Australia.** The Enhanced Critical Infrastructure Risk Management Program Rules 2026 commenced on June 10, 2026, with background checks or Negative Vetting 1 clearances rechecked at least every 5 years for energy assets. Section 4A(6) gives 12 month and 24 month grace periods for different enhanced provisions.

**NIS2, EU.** National transposition is uneven: the Commission sent reasoned opinions to 19 Member States, including Portugal, in May 2025, and Portugal's Decree-Law 125/2025 took effect on April 3, 2026. A January 2026 Commission proposal would make targeted NIS2 amendments.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each utility obligation with its source clause, whether it gates access or a task, and the learning outcome and assessment point that satisfy it. When a standard such as CIP-004-8 becomes enforceable, the affected roles and evidence rules are flagged. See [energy and resources](/industries/energy-resources).

faqs.q: Does CIP-004 training apply to contractors at a utility?
faqs.a: Yes. CIP-004-7 applies to employees, contractors and vendors with authorized electronic access or authorized unescorted physical access to high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems and their associated EACMS and PACS. The training must be complete before access is granted, so contractor onboarding should check the matrix before issuing badges or credentials.

faqs.q: Is a pipeline operator qualification the same as training?
faqs.a: No. PHMSA defines qualified as evaluated and able to perform the covered task and to recognize and react to abnormal operating conditions. Training is required as appropriate, but the evidence is the evaluation. The utility sets the evaluation interval for each covered task and keeps prior qualification records for five years.

faqs.q: Who holds the water operator certificate, the utility or the person?
faqs.a: The individual holds the certificate under a state program, while the system owner must ensure a designated certified operator is available for each operating shift. In the matrix, treat certification as a verification row on the person and shift coverage as a separate row on the utility.

faqs.q: Does the SOCI Act require a specific training course?
faqs.a: No. The CIRMP Rules prescribe no training course and do not use the word training. Training reaches critical workers through the program's duty to minimize risks from negligent employees and contractors and through the cyber framework the entity chooses, such as the AESCSF or the Essential Eight. The utility must justify its training as a control.
